summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Quick Start (2025 Update) - Part 10: UV Editor ## How to Open a UV Editor (UB) Marvelous Designer supports you in opening a UV (UB) according to the shape of the board. Here, I added a seat in advance. 1. Right-click on the 2D board window or the 3D window title bar. 2. Select **Open UB Editor**. You can see that there are two labels at the bottom of the 2D window. You can quickly switch between the 2D window and the UB editor window again. 3. Right-click on the blank area in the UB window to place the UB in the 2D board. ### Tips for Editing UBs **Tip 1:** Before you start editing the UB, it is best to place the UB in the 2D board first. This ensures the correct ratio between UBs and helps organize the UB position. - Use the **Automatic UB Fill Tool** in the upper left corner. - Fill in the desired value to determine the distance between the UB pieces. - Select the **Optimized Layout** option and press and hold to choose whether to allow rotation and set the shrink ratio. This tool will automatically adjust the selected UB pieces to the appropriate size and position them in the first line. ### Aligning UB Pieces To adjust the position of the UB pieces: 1. Select the UB pieces and right-click. 2. You can turn the UB pieces horizontally or vertically and also align them. 3. Then right-click again and place the UB pieces at 0-1. 4. Enter the number in the dialog box at the bottom to determine the distance between the UB pieces and the edge of the UB frame. This operation will mix the selected UB pieces together and fill them into the first UB line. ### Editing UBs on the Back and Side **Tip 2:** If you want to edit the UB on the back and side of the board: 1. Change the texture display on the 3D window to the **Rumi Texture Surface**. This is necessary to identify the UB on the back and side. 2. Select the board, adjust the height, increase the thickness, and zoom in (in mm). This will determine the width of the UB on the side. 3. Pull the **Element Edit** button to the bottom. 4. Open the UB expansion bar and select the UB you want to appear. **Tip 3:** Select the UB on the back and side. At this point, the UB on the back and side will appear in the UB editor. The UB on the back is defaulted to overlap with the UB on the front, while the UB on the side is defaulted to squeeze out along the edge of the UB on the front. ### Overlap and Material Selection **Tip 2:** Experiment with the distance between the UB pieces and the UB frame. The two numbers written below should be greater than the thickness of the fabric. If you open the UB on the side, there will be a cross overlap between the UB pieces. **Tip 3:** If you plan to use different materials on the front and back: - Press **Shift + A** to select all the UB pieces on the front. - Use the **Move UB Tool** to move the UB on the front to other lines. ### Finalizing UB Editing 1. Click on the item you want to use. 2. In the **Property Editor**, switch to the back cover page to cancel the selection of materials that are the same as those on the front. 3. Select the material for the side. **Tip 4:** At this time, the UB editing is basically complete. ### Additional Tools - Click on the small ball in the upper left corner to see the different types of postage effects again. - **Tip 6:** Use the **Baking Pattern Tool** to bake and save the postage you need. - **Tip 7:** Use the **UB Quick Photo Tool** to take a screenshot and save the UB quick photo you need. That's all for today. Thanks for watching, and see you in the next video! ```
